title: Design a File Sync & Storage Service (Dropbox/Google Drive)
prompt: Design a file storage and sync service like Dropbox or Google Drive. Users store files that sync across their devices; edits on one device propagate to others. Cover chunking, deduplication, efficient sync of changed bytes, conflict resolution when two devices edit offline, and the metadata layer. Assume many users with large files and multiple devices each.
blurb: Content-defined chunking, block dedup, delta sync, and the offline-edit conflict problem — the metadata plane is the real system.

rubric.label: Requirements gathering
rubric.description: Separates functional (upload/download, multi-device sync, sharing, versioning, offline edits) from non-functional (sync latency, durability, bandwidth efficiency, consistency model).

rubric.label: Clarifying questions
rubric.description: Asks about file sizes, number of devices, edit frequency, offline support, sharing/collab, storage quotas.

rubric.label: Back-of-envelope estimations
rubric.description: Storage with/without dedup, upload/download bandwidth, metadata QPS, notification fan-out.

rubric.label: Chunking & deduplication depth
rubric.description: Fixed vs content-defined chunking (rolling hash), block hashing, global vs per-user dedup, and only uploading changed chunks. Key senior signal.

rubric.label: Sync protocol depth
rubric.description: How a client detects changes and syncs deltas: local watcher, chunk-diff, upload changed blocks, metadata commit, notify other devices (long-poll/push). Key senior signal.

rubric.label: Conflict resolution
rubric.description: Two devices edit the same file offline: versioning, conflicted copies, last-writer-wins vs merge, causal ordering (version vectors).

rubric.label: API design
rubric.description: list/mutate metadata, block upload/download, commit, subscribe to changes; separation of metadata vs block APIs.

rubric.label: Data model
rubric.description: files/folders metadata tree, file→ordered blocks, block store (hash→data), device cursors/namespaces.

rubric.label: High-level design
rubric.description: Split metadata service from block storage; upload path (chunk→dedup→commit) vs download/sync path (diff→fetch).

rubric.label: Scaling
rubric.description: Sharding metadata by user/namespace, block store on object storage + CDN, notification fan-out scaling.

rubric.label: Bottlenecks
rubric.description: Metadata hot namespaces, notification storm on shared folders, dedup index size, large-file sync amplification.

rubric.label: Consistency & durability
rubric.description: Atomic metadata commits, ordering guarantees per namespace, durable blocks, crash recovery mid-sync.

rubric.label: Observability & security
rubric.description: Sync lag, conflict rate, dedup ratio; encryption at rest/in transit, sharing ACLs.

functional_requirements: Sync files across a user's multiple devices
Efficient sync: only transfer changed bytes/blocks
Offline edits that reconcile on reconnect
Conflict handling when two devices edit the same file
nonfunctional_requirements: Low sync latency (edit visible on other devices in seconds)
Strong consistency on metadata within a namespace; ordered updates
Scales to large files and many devices per user
clarifying_questions: Typical and max file sizes? Many small files or few large ones?
How many devices per user, and is offline editing a first-class requirement?
Do we need real-time collaborative editing, or file-level sync?
Is sharing at file or folder granularity, and with external users?
Do we keep full version history and for how long?
Global dedup across users or per-user only (privacy/security)?
qualifying_questions: Do we need end-to-end encryption (which constrains server-side dedup)?
Expected read:write ratio and edit hot-spots (shared team folders)?
Client platforms and their local FS-watch capabilities?

estimations.traffic: 100M users, avg 100K files each. Edits: say 10M active users × a few file changes/day. Metadata QPS dominated by list/poll: millions of clients long-polling for changes.
estimations.storage: Raw could be exabytes; block-level dedup + compression can cut 30-50%+ for common content. Blocks in object storage; metadata (much smaller) in a sharded transactional store.
estimations.bandwidth: Delta sync means only changed ~4MB chunks move, not whole files — a 1-byte change in a 1GB file transfers one chunk, not 1GB.
estimations.notifications: A shared folder with 1000 members changing → fan-out notifications to up to 1000 devices; must batch/coalesce.

core_components: Client agent (FS watcher, chunker, local index)
data_model: namespaces(ns_id, owner, type) — a user's root or a shared folder; unit of ordering/sharing
files(file_id, ns_id, path, size, latest_version, is_dir, updated_at)
file_versions(file_id, version, block_list[ordered block_hashes], device_id, parent_version, vector)
blocks(block_hash PK, size, storage_url, refcount) — content-addressed, deduped
device_cursors(device_id, ns_id, last_seen_seq) — where each device is in the change log
changes(ns_id, seq, file_id, version, op) — ordered per-namespace change log
api_design: GET /v1/ns/{ns_id}/delta?cursor=<seq> → { changes[], new_cursor } (list changed files since cursor)
POST /v1/blocks { hashes[] } → { missing_hashes[] } (which blocks to actually upload)
POST /v1/files/{id}/commit { block_list, parent_version, device_id } → { version } or 409 conflict
Long-poll GET /v1/ns/{ns_id}/subscribe?cursor= → wakes when new changes exist
reference.high_level_design: The system is split into a METADATA plane and a BLOCK plane. Client agent: a local file watcher detects a change, splits the file into chunks using content-defined chunking (rolling hash so an insert only shifts one chunk boundary), hashes each chunk, and asks the block service which hashes are missing (dedup — unchanged/duplicate blocks aren't re-uploaded). It uploads only missing blocks to the block store (object storage), then commits new metadata (ordered block list + parent version) to the metadata service. The metadata service assigns a monotonic per-namespace sequence number, appends to that namespace's change log, and notifies other devices via the notification service. Other devices long-poll /delta with their cursor, learn which files changed, fetch only the missing blocks, and reassemble. Downloads come from object storage/CDN. Conflicts are detected at commit by comparing parent_version / version vectors.

deep_dives.probe: Why content-defined chunking with a rolling hash instead of fixed-size blocks? Show me what happens to the chunk boundaries and the upload set when a user inserts one byte at the start of a large file. How does the missing-block negotiation work, and do you dedup globally or per user — what's the security concern with global dedup?

Walk me end to end through syncing an edit from device A to device B: local detection, chunk diff, block upload, metadata commit, sequencing, and how B learns and pulls only the changed blocks. How do devices resume after being offline for a week?

Two devices edit the same file offline, then both come online. How do you detect the conflict at commit, and what do you do — last-writer-wins, a conflicted copy, or merge? How do version vectors / parent_version give you causal ordering rather than guessing by timestamp?
A shared team folder has 1000 members. One person adds a file. How do you notify all their devices without a thundering herd, and how do long-poll subscribers scale to millions of idle connections?

You cache namespace metadata / delta responses and popular block locations. A widely-shared folder's cache entry expires while thousands of devices are polling it. How do you avoid a stampede recomputing the delta — coalescing, jittered TTL, logical expiry?

File metadata lives in your transactional metadata store but needs to feed full-text search and sharing/audit systems. How do you propagate changes — CDC/Debezium off the metadata DB vs dual writes — while preserving per-namespace ordering?

followup_bank.question: Fixed vs content-defined chunking? Show the boundary behavior when a byte is inserted mid-file, and how the missing-block negotiation avoids re-uploading unchanged data.
How do you detect the conflict deterministically (version vectors / parent_version) rather than relying on wall-clock timestamps, and what's the user-visible resolution?
Eviction policy for delta/metadata cache — TTL vs LRU? How do you prevent a stampede when a widely-shared folder's cached delta expires under many polling clients?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions database or metadata store or sql
followup_bank.question: How do metadata changes reach search/audit — CDC/Debezium vs dual writes — while keeping per-namespace ordering intact?
Global vs per-user dedup — what's the privacy/security tradeoff, and how do you refcount blocks so deleting one file doesn't drop shared blocks?

followup_bank.trigger: mentions notification or poll or push
followup_bank.question: How do you fan out change notifications to a 1000-member shared folder without a thundering herd, and scale millions of idle long-poll connections?

scaling: Shard metadata by namespace/user; ordering guaranteed per namespace
Blocks on horizontally scalable object storage + CDN for downloads
Batch/coalesce notifications; scale long-poll with lightweight connection servers
Dedup index sharded by block-hash prefix
bottlenecks: Notification fan-out storm on large shared folders
Dedup index size and lookup cost at exabyte scale
Large-file sync amplification without good chunking
tradeoffs: Content-defined chunking (insert-resilient, variable size, more CPU) vs fixed-size (simple, shifts on insert)
Global dedup (max storage savings, cross-user privacy risk / confirmation attacks) vs per-user dedup (safer, less savings)
Last-writer-wins (simple, data loss) vs conflicted copies (safe, user friction) vs merge (best UX, only for known formats)
Strong per-namespace consistency vs cross-namespace eventual
Push notifications (instant, connection cost) vs long-poll (simpler, latency)
alternative_solutions: Operational Transform / CRDTs for real-time collaborative editing (vs file-level sync)
rsync-style delta encoding within a chunk for fine-grained diffs
Merkle-tree file manifests to diff directory trees quickly
Client-side end-to-end encryption with per-user (not global) dedup
observability: Sync end-to-end lag (edit → visible on other device)
Notification delivery latency and long-poll connection counts
security: Encryption in transit and at rest
ACL enforcement on sharing; capability tokens for shared links
Per-user dedup or careful design to avoid cross-user existence leaks
Virus/malware scanning; ransomware detection via version history
Rate limiting; audit logs on shares
reference.reference_answer: A strong answer cleanly separates the metadata plane from the block plane and makes the client agent do content-defined chunking (rolling hash) so a mid-file insert only re-uploads one chunk. It negotiates missing blocks against a content-addressed, refcounted, deduped block store, then commits an ordered block-list version to the metadata service, which assigns a per-namespace monotonic sequence and notifies other devices that pull only changed blocks via a cursor-based /delta. Conflicts are detected at commit via parent_version / version vectors (causal, not timestamp-based) and resolved with conflicted copies or merge. The candidate scales notifications with batching/coalescing and lightweight long-poll servers, shards metadata by namespace with strict per-namespace ordering, handles the shared-folder cache stampede, propagates metadata to search/audit via CDC, and reasons about the global-vs-per-user dedup privacy tradeoff. Top bottlenecks: notification fan-out, hot namespaces, and dedup index size, each with mitigations.

interviewer_notes: The trap is treating this as 'upload files to S3' — the depth is in chunking/dedup, delta sync, and conflict resolution. Push the chunking deep-dive with the one-byte-insert scenario to see if they know why content-defined chunking beats fixed blocks. Drive the sync protocol end-to-end (missing-block negotiation, per-namespace sequencing, cursor delta) and force a real conflict-resolution answer using version vectors, not timestamps. Use the cache/stampede probe on shared-folder deltas and the CDC probe when metadata feeds search/audit. Bonus signal: refcounting blocks for deletes, global-vs-per-user dedup privacy, and notification fan-out on large shared folders. Reserve time for consistency/durability and security.
